extract:
Nasir Jones, known professionally as Nas, was born in Brooklyn in 1973 and raised in the Queensbridge Houses in Long Island City, Queens — at the time the largest public housing development in North America and a fertile breeding ground for hip-hop talent following the success of Marley Marl and the Juice Crew. The son of jazz cornetist Olu Dara, Nas dropped out of school in the eighth grade and immersed himself in the local rap scene, drawing inspiration from Queensbridge predecessors like MC Shan and Roxanne Shanté, as well as Rakim's lyrical dexterity. His first appearance came in 1991 on Main Source's "Live at the Barbeque," produced by Large Professor, where his opening verse made him an immediate object of fascination among New York rap insiders.

That buzz culminated in his 1994 debut album Illmatic, released on Columbia Records, which assembled an unprecedented roster of producers — DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip, Large Professor, and L.E.S. — across a tight ten tracks. Songs like "N.Y. State of Mind," "The World Is Yours," "Life's a Bitch" (featuring AZ and a trumpet solo from his father), and "One Love" set a new bar for street poetry, and the album is now routinely cited as one of the greatest hip-hop records ever made. His follow-up, It Was Written (1996), produced largely by Trackmasters, pivoted toward a more commercial, mafioso-rap aesthetic and yielded the hit "If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)" with Lauryn Hill, going multi-platinum despite a more divided critical reception.

The late 1990s and early 2000s saw Nas form the short-lived supergroup The Firm with AZ, Foxy Brown, and Nature, and release a string of albums including I Am... (1999), Nastradamus (1999), and Stillmatic (2001). The latter was widely seen as a creative resurgence, fueled in part by his high-profile feud with Jay-Z, whose "Takeover" Nas answered with the scorching "Ether." He continued with God's Son (2002) and the double album Street's Disciple (2004), then signed to Def Jam — then helmed by Jay-Z — and released Hip Hop Is Dead in 2006, a polemical state-of-the-genre record. His 2008 untitled album, originally announced under a more incendiary title, tackled race in America directly on tracks like "Sly Fox" and "Black President."

Nas's collaborative 2010 album with reggae artist Damian Marley, Distant Relatives, channeled proceeds toward African charities and broadened his thematic range. After Life Is Good (2012), a reflective record built around his divorce from singer Kelis, he entered a prolific late-career phase working extensively with Kanye West, who produced the seven-track Nasir (2018) as part of the Wyoming sessions, and Hit-Boy, with whom he made the King's Disease trilogy (2020–2022) and Magic series. King's Disease won him his first competitive Grammy for Best Rap Album in 2021, after decades of nominations.

Beyond music, Nas co-founded the venture capital firm QueensBridge Venture Partners, with early investments in Ridesharing, Dropbox, and Coinbase, and launched the Mass Appeal media and record label. He remains an active recording artist and a defining figure of East Coast hip-hop, his Queensbridge origins and Illmatic-era verses still serving as a touchstone for lyrical craft in rap.
title: Nas
